Subject: Unusually high trial signups — can you pause auto-credits?

Hi Mina,

We're running a small internal onboarding at Cascade Tech and noticed ~15 new trial accounts got auto-credit grants in the last 12 hours. A few of these appear to be from disposable emails and some share the same user-agent string which looks odd. Our security team tagged it as possibly automated signups.

Can you pause the auto-issuance for the cascadetech.com domain and advise on whether you can reverse credits for accounts created in the last 24 hours? We're worried about credits being used before we can confirm legitimate users.

Our account id: CAS-7421.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor

Subject: Re: Unusually high trial signups — initial triage

Quick triage below (ran on the CSV):
- Total new trial accounts in window: 15
- Cluster of 8 accounts with disposable email providers (mailinator, yopmail).
- 7 accounts show identical browser fingerprint hashes and UA string "Chrome/118.0.5993"; IPs are not identical but map to the same cloud provider ASN (possible proxy pool).
- 2 accounts match previously verified employee emails (sarah@cascadetech.com, ryan@cascadetech.com) based on past invoices and SSO logs. Recommend preserving those.

Recommendation:
1) Revoke credits for the 7 highest-confidence suspicious accounts.
2) Hold credits for the remaining unverified accounts pending manual verification.
3) Issue two manual trial extensions/credits to the verified users while we finish cleanup.

I've exported quick screenshots of the signup dashboard (screenshot-signup-dashboard.png) and attached a filtered CSV with flags. If you want me to run a deeper device-fingerprint diff, I can export the audit logs.

--Aditya

Subject: Re: Unusually high trial signups — additional signals and suggested mitigations

Adding additional signal context and a mitigation plan: 
- Device fingerprint analysis: 9 accounts share 3 nearly-identical fingerprint hashes (same canvas, WebGL, timezone, and extensions sequence) — strongly indicates automated client.
- Timing patterns: spikes at ~03:00 UTC in 30s bursts (bot-like).
- Email entropy: the disposable addresses have low-entropy local parts and registration timestamps within 1 minute of each other.

Suggested immediate changes (self-serve pipeline):
- Add throttling rule for new signups originating from the same ASN within a 1-hour window for unverified domains.
- Introduce lightweight CAPTCHA challenge on email-only signups for domains without prior SSO/paid history.
- Flag and delay auto-credits for domains with >5 new accounts in 24 hours until manual review.

Operational steps I can perform now:
- Prepare an admin rollback (link below) to revoke credits for specific account ids.
- Export audit log slice to confirm token usage (attached: audit-log-export.json stub).

Admin rollback link: https://app.redwood.ai/admin/rollbacks/HP-7421
